prompt_text: My air conditioning needs fixing in Phoenix. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
competitors_mentioned: Check the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC)
answer_verbatim:
I can give specific companies — but first a couple quick questions so the recommendations match your location and urgency:

- What’s your ZIP code (or neighborhood) in Phoenix?
- Is this an emergency (no cooling / health risk) or a non‑urgent repair?
- Is it a residential or commercial unit, and do you know the brand/model?

If you want an immediate action plan, read the short checklist below. If you reply with your ZIP and whether it’s urgent, I’ll give a tailored short list of reputable contractors near you and exactly what to ask them.

Immediate steps (if it’s an emergency)
- If anyone is at risk from heat, call 911 or get to a cooling center.
- Turn the thermostat up a few degrees and set the fan to ON to circulate air.
- If the system is blowing hot air, turn the compressor breaker off for a few minutes and then back on to see if a reset helps — only if you’re comfortable doing so.
- Don’t open the cabinet or touch refrigerant lines if you’re not trained.

Who to call and why (how I’ll choose them for you)
- National/local 24/7 emergency service: good for nights/weekends and quick dispatch.
- Manufacturer‑authorized dealers (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Goodman, etc.): best when you need warranty work or brand‑specific parts/diagnostics.
- Large regional firms with in‑house parts and many technicians: faster same‑day service and ongoing maintenance plans.
- Highly rated local independent companies: often lower cost and more personalized service; choose ones with many recent 4–5 star reviews and strong BBB/Angi ratings.
- Utility‑partner contractors: can help with rebates/energy‑efficiency inspections (APS, SRP).

Examples of reputable options commonly available in Phoenix
- Goettl Air Conditioning & Plumbing — Phoenix‑based, long history in the valley; typically offers same‑day service and has experience with Phoenix‑specific cooling issues.
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (local Phoenix franchise) — national brand with 24/7 emergency service and flat‑rate pricing in many locations.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (local branch) — large company with extensive staffing for rapid dispatch and maintenance plans.
- Manufacturer dealer for your unit (e.g., Carrier, Trane, Lennox): look up “Carrier dealer Phoenix” (or your brand) for authorized techs who can do warranty repairs.

(If you prefer only local independents, I’ll narrow to well‑rated Phoenix independents once you give ZIP.)

What to ask when you call
- Are you licensed with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors? What is your license number?
- Are your techs NATE‑certified and EPA 608 certified?
- Do you charge a diagnostic/trip fee? How much?
- Do you offer a written estimate and a parts/labor warranty?
- Can you do same‑day service and do you offer 24/7 emergency response?
- Do you honor manufacturer warranties / are you an authorized dealer for my brand?

How to verify before hiring
- Check the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) for the contractor’s license and status.
- Read recent Google, Yelp, and BBB reviews (look for patterns, not single reviews).
- Confirm any quoted warranty in writing.

If you tell me your ZIP code and whether it’s urgent, I’ll reply with 4–6 specific contractors near you (a mix of 24/7, manufacturer‑authorized, regional, and top‑rated independents) plus the best one to call first for your situation.
